passages.provision_quote: Sec. 2. (a) A school shall notify in writing at least one (1) parent of a student, if the student is an unemancipated minor, of a request made by the student to change the student's: (1) name; or (2) pronoun, title, or word to identify the student.
passages.note: Enrolled act text of the instrument Raatz sponsored and voted for; the new chapter states the notification duty, and no section of the act creates a danger exception to it.

rows.reasoning: As a Senate sponsor of HB 1608 (2023) and a Yea on its third-reading passage, Raatz acted on an instrument whose new chapter provides that "A school shall notify in writing at least one (1) parent of a student" of a request to change the student's name or pronoun, within five business days. That duty runs to every such request and the act carries no exception for staff who believe notice would endanger the student — its savings clauses preserve only the child-abuse reporting duty and federal law, and SECTIONS 1 and 2 subordinate school counselor and psychologist privilege to the duty — so it matches "Require staff to notify parents whenever a student asks to be treated as a different gender at school" rather than the rung with a safety exception. The act requires written notice, not consent, so it is not "Require written parental permission before staff use a student's chosen name or pronouns".
